To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TME value of a lipid source depends on the diet in which it is used.
the basal diet composition, the level of input, and the fatty acid profile of the diet affect the utilization of beef fat as a source for TME.
the utilization of tallow as a source of energy and lipid was influenced by the basal diet.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an experimental model to study the utilization of fats as a source of TME, lipid, and specific fatty acids.
the utilization of fat by adult male cockerels.
the effect of diet and level of fat input on the utilization of a fat source.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tallow is a good source of TME and lipid for poultry.
dietary composition and the level of fat in the diet affect the utilization of tallow by adult chickens.
the composition of the basal diet has a marked influence on the utilization of tallow as a source of TME, lipid, and individual fatty acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TME value of beef tallow is affected by the basal diet and the level of tallowed input.
a high corn basal diet permitted the greatest utilization of beef tallowed to adult cockerels and that a supplement of soy lecithins to a wheat basal was equally effective.
the utilization of tallow as a source of TME, lipid, and unsaturated fatty acids is influenced by dietary factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
diet composition can affect the utilization of fat by chickens.
the TME bio-assay is a useful tool for measuring the availability of lipid and fatty acids in poultry feeds.
the TME value of fat is influenced by the diet and the basal diet should be considered when evaluating the value of fat.
